title: Yusuf in one sitting, part two
hookLine: Surah 12:58–111, from the brothers to the fulfilled dream
tomorrow: a few young men run for a cave. what do they pray at its mouth?

lines: HE KNOWS THEM. THEY DON'T KNOW HIM.
cards: Hana is coming over tonight to see Dadi. It's the first time since the bangles, and Amira has rehearsed three openings in the shower.
In the surah, the brothers walk into Egypt hungry, asking for grain, and stand in front of the man they threw into a well. He knows them at once. They have no idea who he is.
He has the storehouses, the power, every reason. So what does he do?

teach.b: He feeds them first. He asks them to bring the youngest brother, and when they do, a royal cup turns up in the youngest's bag, and the story tightens.
Back home, Ya'qub has wept until his eyes went white with grief, and he still sends his sons out with a command not to despair of Allah's mercy.
They return to Yusuf, humbled, and he asks them if they know what they did to Yusuf.

teach.h: I AM JOSEPH AND THIS IS MY BROTHER.
teach.b: Then, in Pickthall's words: "I am Joseph and this is my brother." They confess. And he says: no blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.
His shirt is laid on his father's face, and Ya'qub sees again.
The whole family bows, and Yusuf says the dream from the start has come true.
Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: tradition says that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, entered Mecca, before the people who had driven him out, he gave them Yusuf's words.
No blame on you today. The best of stories, finished in mercy.

how: Muslims read Surah Yusuf whole, and 'no blame on you today', la tathriba 'alaykum al-yawm, is quoted when a wrong is forgiven without reproach.

games.q: what does “yusuf in one sitting” mean?
o: a fast kept in memory of Yusuf's years in prison
Surah Yusuf read whole, ending in forgiveness
the Bible's Joseph chapters read aloud at a mosque

games.q: part two of the story — tap the pairs.
p: come to Egypt hungry, for grain

s: Yusuf took his revenge on his brothers before forgiving them
he fed them, tested them, and at the reveal said: no blame on you today; may Allah forgive you.
in the Qur'an, Yusuf's shirt brings back his father's sight
laid on Ya'qub's face, it restores his sight, and the family comes to Egypt.

games.q: a guy who once stole from your dad's coffee shop comes back, broke, asking for work. your dad asks what you think. what does Yusuf's part two model?
o: meet him without shaming him, and look at what's right now.
make him pay back every dollar first; then the past is clear.
turn him away; forgiving means you never have to see him.
games.why: Yusuf held every card and said no blame on you today. the surah doesn't say pretend nothing happened; it says don't reproach.

practice: Think of one person you owe a first word to, the way Yusuf spoke first. Type the opening line of that message on your phone, just one line, and hold it in your hand for the sit. Sending it is a choice for later.

wordCard.voice: Yusuf in one sitting: the whole surah, from a boy's dream to a family bowing, finished in mercy.

orig.note: Arabic: no blame on you today, Yusuf's words to his brothers in 12:92.

carryVoice: For the week's end: no blame on you today, said by the one who could have blamed. Two weeks, whole.

sources.q: I am Joseph and this is my brother.

sources.ref: Qur'an 12:58–111 (the brothers come for grain; the youngest brother; the cup; Ya'qub's grief and 'despair not of the Spirit of Allah' (12:87); the reveal; 'no blame on you today' (12:92); the shirt and the sight (12:93–96); the dream fulfilled (12:100))
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (as transmitted by Ibn Hisham), on the conquest of Mecca: 'no blame on you today'
